title: HSL and HSLA
learningObjectives: Explain hsl and hsla and apply it correctly in a small CSS example.

understand.concept: The hsl() function describes colour using hue, saturation, and lightness. Hue is an angle on a colour wheel, saturation describes intensity, and lightness describes how light or dark the colour is. Alpha can be added with a slash, for example hsl(210 70% 45% / 80%).
understand.whyItMatters: Hue is commonly represented from 0 to 360 degrees. Saturation and lightness are percentages. HSL can make it easier to create related shades by changing lightness while keeping hue and saturation similar.
understand.analogy: HSL is like choosing a position on a colour wheel, then adjusting vividness and brightness. It is a useful editing model, not a complete model of human colour perception.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy helps build intuition, but the browser follows the CSS specifications and computed-style rules rather than human intentions.

explain.narrative: The three swatches keep a similar hue while lightness changes. Edit the hue angle from 205 to 145 degrees.

examples.explanation: The three swatches keep a similar hue while lightness changes. Edit the hue angle from 205 to 145 degrees.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered demonstration of the CSS concept described in the lesson.

practise.guidedTask: Build a three-colour theme by keeping hue constant and changing lightness. Record the HSL values.
practise.independentTask: Which HSL component is expressed as an angle?

Add unrelated declarations until it looks right
